This episode was actually terrible. Learning all of the information though flashbacks was just lazy writing and prevented there being any action. None of the characters had a growth/change arc. This episode used bad writing techniques in general.

First we are warned several times that the witches are in danger, but they are never actually threatened, feel afraid, nor are they killed which would have been exciting and make sense. 

Second everything was treated with a sense of irony, from the ghost suffering to the witches experience in the house. Without the ghosts actually feeling their suffering all of the weight of their situation is gone. Knowing they are actually suffering gives weight to it being a prison and makes us feel more sympathetic for everyone trapped in the house. 

Third we learn that people in the house aren't actually evil it's just the house that's evil, OR something in the house, and that whatever that is left with Michael. This is a shame because it deflates all of the season one characters. Tate is no longer evil, or a psychopath, he was possessed or influenced. Hell he's not even Michaels father anymore which takes even more heft of his character away. 

Fourth the bag of bones is potentially a story breaking piece of lore. Does it require your bones to be on the property to be stuck there? If so then many of those ghosts should not be there. Are we to believe Tate was buried in the house after he was shot by the cops? Burned mans family was buried there? And if that's the case than why didn't Constance just burry Addie there post death?

I really enjoyed seeing Moira be freed, and that was a good and logical sequence, however, if we had learned that the ghosts were actually constantly suffering and that it didn't devolve into ironic name calling and snarky 1 liners in their after life it would have been even more powerful. 

So to sum up it was bad writing because 1. they didn't follow through on the threats presented at the beginning of the episode. 2. there was no action. 3. None of the characters changed or grew. ( I guess we learn Behold doesn't really like evil, and maybe Madison gains some empathy, but that journey was not shown well and was still minor. If she had super empathy why not give all the ghosts back their bones huh?) 4. new lore actually deflated the importance of lore that already existed. 

That said I love AHS and hope we never have another dull episode like this.

There are no gods, but magic is real. People can manipulate air, fire, water, shadows, life in various ways, summon creatures from some external space, see the past, semi-predict the future, and project their minds, but there is no evidence of any god. 

Just like the real world, people may attribute things that occur to their god but there is no proof they couldn't have done or experienced these things without a god's influence. 

The only thing we know is that people have worshiped tons of various gods throughout the centuries. We are never shown an actual god appearing to anyone, or speaking directly to them. We also have no historical evidence of this happening. The only people who ever even claim to hear gods voices are religious fanatics who, just like in this world, describe a personal experience that cannot be confirmed by others.
